name: Argentina
gaps: Jujuy, Formosa, La Rioja, San Juan, and Mendoza: COAs exist but specific contact URLs not readily available. Misiones, Corrientes, Salta, Tucumán, Santa Fe, Santiago del Estero, Entre Ríos: Multiple COAs active but individual club websites difficult to locate; refer to Aves Argentinas coordination email.

Dropped for lack of a presence of their own: eBird Argentina (eBird region page, not a community); COA Guaicurú in Chaco (no presence of its own, shares the national umbrella's URL); COA Ushuaia in Tierra del Fuego (no presence of its own, shares the national umbrella's URL)
Dropped, the social page cited did not exist (soft 404 behind a 200): COA Las Lajas; COA Sierras Chicas; COA Sietecolores Lago Pellegrini; COA Diucón; COA Ñamco

groups.name: Aves Argentinas
groups.blurb: The national bird society and BirdLife partner, coordinating 80 plus local bird club chapters across Argentina.

groups.name: CoaRECS
groups.blurb: Club de Observadores de Aves of Costanera Sur Ecological Reserve, Buenos Aires, with directory of 97 COAs.

groups.name: COA Carancho
groups.blurb: Bird watching club in Palermo neighbourhood, Buenos Aires, running urban birding walks and outings.

groups.name: COA Tucúquere Bariloche
groups.blurb: Regional bird watchers club in Bariloche, promoting observation, education and habitat conservation.

groups.name: COA Tintica
groups.blurb: Bird observers club at Villa La Angostura, Neuquén, organising field walks and species surveys.

groups.name: COA Huet Huet
groups.blurb: Patagonian bird club in Neuquén with regular outings and local birding community activities.

groups.name: COA Ñandú
groups.blurb: Regional bird observers club in San Luis province with walks and environmental education.

groups.name: COA Catamarca
groups.blurb: Regional bird club affiliated with Aves Argentinas, coordinating observation activities in Catamarca.

name: Bolivia
gaps: Limited formal bird club infrastructure; most activity coordinated through national organizations. Regional bird watching groups exist informally but lack public web presence beyond Facebook.

groups.name: Asociación Armonía
groups.blurb: The BirdLife partner in Bolivia since 1993, protecting threatened bird species through 28 strategic reserves and community work.

groups.name: Asociación Boliviana de Ornitología (ASBOR)
groups.blurb: Formed 2007, bringing together ornithologists and bird enthusiasts for research, conservation and citizen science.

groups.name: Club Ornitológico de La Paz Cóndores
groups.blurb: Local bird watching club in La Paz running field trips and coordination for the annual October Big Day event.

name: Brazil
gaps: WikiAves (citizen science platform) could not be URL-verified due to Cloudflare access restrictions, though it is clearly active and is the primary birding platform in Brazil.
Pará and Amazonas have limited findable local bird clubs with public websites; birdwatching activity is primarily tourism and guide-based rather than organized clubs.
Amapá: no local bird clubs with independent online presence found.
Maranhão and Piauí: no local bird clubs with independent online presence found.
Several regional clubs lack active websites and maintain only social media presence (e.g., COA Santos on Instagram, COACGR on Facebook).
Some older URLs from ABOA directory (Multiply, Yahoo Groups, Geocities) are no longer accessible.

Dropped for having no presence of their own, each pointing at the same national COA directory rather than a page of its own: Vem Passarinhar Sampa (São Paulo); Observadores de Aves de Ubatuba (São Paulo); COA Foz do Iguaçu (Paraná); OAA (Paraná); COAVE (Santa Catarina); Santa Catarina Birdwatching (Santa Catarina); Projeto Charão (Rio Grande do Sul); Projeto Cardeal Amarelo (Rio Grande do Sul); Avis Vigilanti (Minas Gerais); COA-JF (Minas Gerais); S.O.S. Falconiformes (Minas Gerais); Amigos das Aves (Rio de Janeiro); Clube de Observadores de Aves da Bahia (Bahia); ANO (Bahia)
Dropped as a global platform rather than a local community (listed once under International): eBird Brasil
Dropped, link dead when checked on 2026-08-09: COAB (São Paulo)

groups.name: SBO

groups.name: ABOA
groups.blurb: Associação Brasileira de Observadores de Aves, national association founded 2011 bringing together birders across Brazil with resources and coordination.

groups.name: SAVE Brasil
groups.blurb: The BirdLife International partner in Brazil, conservation focused organisation operating in ten states with habitat restoration and community engagement.

groups.name: COA Brasil
groups.blurb: National movement and support network for bird observers across Brazil, connecting local clubs and enthusiasts practicing bird observation.

groups.name: Vem Passarinhar
groups.blurb: Nationwide initiative promoting free public bird watching outings in parks and protected areas.

groups.name: OBSERVAVES
groups.blurb: Observadores de Aves do Planalto Central, group founded 2005 promoting birdwatching in the Federal District through training and field excursions.

groups.name: Clube das Aves
groups.blurb: Student organization at Universidade Católica de Brasília dedicated to bird watching and ornithological studies for university community and students.

groups.name: OIA
groups.blurb: Observadores de aves de Goiás, group created by UFG professors and researchers to promote the state's bird fauna and environmental education.

groups.name: GOA Sinop

groups.name: COA Campo Grande

groups.name: CEO

groups.name: COAPI
groups.blurb: Clube de Observação de Aves do Parque Ibirapuera, group based at the iconic São Paulo park offering bird observation education and guided activities.

groups.name: Clube de Observadores de Aves Sesc São Paulo
groups.blurb: Bird watching club run by Sesc in São Paulo providing club activities, field trips and bird observation opportunities for members and visitors.

groups.name: COAVAP
groups.blurb: Clube de Observadores de Aves do Vale do Paraíba, regional group serving the Paraíba Valley region of São Paulo state.

groups.name: COAFRANCA

groups.name: GOA Jundiaí
groups.blurb: Grupo de Observação de Aves de Jundiaí, community group for bird observation in the city of Jundiaí.

groups.name: Associação Viçosense de Observadores de Aves
groups.blurb: Bird watching association based in Viçosa region, connecting local birders for field observations and species documentation.

groups.name: COAMA
groups.blurb: Clube dos Observadores de Aves da Mata Atlântica, group focused on Atlantic Forest bird observation in the region.

groups.name: Observando Aves na Cidade de São Paulo
groups.blurb: Public Facebook group for birders observing and sharing bird sightings in São Paulo city, with active community discussion.

groups.name: GOA Campinas
groups.blurb: Grupo de Observadores de Aves de Campinas, regional group in the city of Campinas for bird observation and community participation.

groups.name: COA-NPR
groups.blurb: Clube de Observadores de Aves Norte do Paraná, regional club in northern Paraná active in Global Big Day and bird observation events.

groups.name: COA Joinville
groups.blurb: Clube de Observadores de Aves de Joinville e Regiao, well established regional club in Santa Catarina running walks and community activities.

groups.name: COA-POA

groups.name: ECOAVIS
groups.blurb: Ecologia e Observação de Aves de Belo Horizonte, group dedicated to bird ecology and observation in Minas Gerais with research focus.

groups.name: COA-ES
groups.blurb: Clube de Observadores de Aves do Espírito Santo, regional club maintaining a directory of COA clubs across Brazil on their website.

groups.name: AMOAVES
groups.blurb: Associação dos Observadores de Aves de Domingos Martins, local group in Espírito Santo for bird observation and community engagement.

groups.name: COA-RJ
groups.blurb: Clube de Observadores de Aves Rio de Janeiro, founded 1985, one of Brazil's oldest COA clubs with active field work and community programs.

groups.name: COA Sul-Fluminense
groups.blurb: Clube dos observadores de aves do Sul Fluminense, regional group for the southern region of Rio de Janeiro state.

groups.name: LORMA
groups.blurb: Laboratório de Ornitologia e Mastozoologia at UEFS, academic research group conducting ornithological studies and bird monitoring in Bahia.

groups.name: OAP
groups.blurb: Observadores de Aves de Pernambuco, group established 1986 bringing together amateur bird observers across the state.

groups.name: Projeto Vem Passarinhar Recife
groups.blurb: Free public monthly bird watching initiative coordinated by environmental activist Ludmila Portela, running guided tours in Recife parks with provided binoculars.

groups.name: Projeto Vem Passarinhar CE
groups.blurb: Initiative launched 2019 organizing free monthly public bird watching outings at Cocó Park and across Ceará's protected areas for community environmental education.

groups.name: GOP
groups.blurb: Grupo Ornitológico Potiguar, founded 2007 in Natal, group conducting ornithological research and documentation of Rio Grande do Norte birds.

name: Chile
gaps: Regional nuclei beyond Valparaíso, Metropolitan, and Los Lagos have limited online documentation. Atacama, Coquimbo, Bio Bio, Araucania, and southern regions lack identified club websites or Facebook pages with current activity.

Dropped for lack of a presence of their own: eBird Chile (eBird region page, not a community); Núcleo ROC Valparaíso in Valparaíso (no presence of its own, shares the national umbrella's URL); Núcleo ROC RM in Metropolitan Region (no presence of its own, shares the national umbrella's URL); Núcleo ROC Los Lagos in Los Lagos (no presence of its own, shares the national umbrella's URL)
Dropped, the social page cited did not exist (soft 404 behind a 200): Grupo de Ornitólogos del Maule

groups.name: Red de Observadores de Aves y Vida Silvestre
groups.blurb: The national bird and wildlife observer network and BirdLife partner, coordinating citizen science and conservation across Chile.

groups.name: Unión de Ornitólogos de Chile
groups.blurb: Professional ornithological union promoting bird conservation, publishing the Revista Chilena de Ornitología.

name: Colombia
gaps: Meta, Casanare, Arauca, Vichada, Guaviare, Guainía departments have few findable groups with own sites; mostly rely on national RNOA network or Global Big Day coordination.
Dropped, link dead when checked on 2026-08-09: Fondo Filantrópico ATA (Countrywide); Asociación Río Cali (Valle del Cauca)

groups.name: Asociación Calidris
groups.blurb: The BirdLife partner in Colombia, studying and conserving birds and their habitats through research and field work across the country.

groups.name: ProAves
groups.blurb: The largest private reserve system in Colombia protecting endangered species and 68 percent of threatened birds through conservation and ecotourism.

groups.name: Red Nacional de Observadores de Aves (RNOA)
groups.blurb: National network coordinating cooperation and information exchange among regional ornithological associations and bird observers.

groups.name: Asociación Colombiana de Ornitología (ACO)
groups.blurb: Scientific society founded 2002 advancing study and conservation of Colombian birds through publication and research.

groups.name: Global Big Day Colombia
groups.blurb: Organizing committee coordinating thousands of birdwatchers across Colombia for the annual global citizen science event.

groups.name: Pajareritos
groups.blurb: Foundation introducing children to bird observation and conservation through education and guided outings.

groups.name: Guardián de las Aves
groups.blurb: Children's conservation programme connecting young people to birds and environmental protection nationwide.

groups.name: Instituto Humboldt
groups.blurb: National research institute for biological diversity and ecosystems, supporting ornithological research and conservation.

groups.name: Asociación Bogotana de Ornitología (ABO)
groups.blurb: Nonprofit dedicated to bird conservation and study in Bogotá and surrounding regions through bird walks and counts.

groups.name: Grupo Observadores de Aves Universidad Nacional (GOUN)
groups.blurb: University ornithology group promoting bird study and observation among students and researchers in Bogotá.

groups.name: Sociedad Caldense de Ornitología
groups.blurb: Founded 1984, second oldest ornithological society in Colombia, studying and defending birds in Caldas department.

groups.name: Sociedad Quindíana de Ornitología
groups.blurb: Regional ornithology society coordinating bird observation and conservation in the Coffee Triangle region.

groups.name: Sociedad Antioqueña de Ornitología (SAO)
groups.blurb: Founded 1984 with 210 members, publishing the oldest indexed ornithological journal in Colombia (SAO Bulletin).

groups.name: Sociedad Ornitológica de Córdoba (SOC)
groups.blurb: Founded 2019, discovering new species and running the Agami Heron community birding trail in coastal Caribbean.

groups.name: Fundación Ornitológica del Atlántico (ORNIAT)
groups.blurb: Founded 1998, studying Atlantic department birds and promoting bird observation through school field guides.

groups.name: Asociación Ornitológica de Boyacá (Ixobrychus)
groups.blurb: Regional ornithology association studying and conserving birds across Boyacá department.

groups.name: Fundación Ecológica Los Colibríes (FELCA)
groups.blurb: Founded 1991, protecting 12000 hectares of forest in Nariño and discovering 30 species new to science.

groups.name: Asociación Gaica
groups.blurb: Research and conservation organization working on biodiversity and ornithology in southwestern Colombia.

name: Ecuador
gaps: Regional ornithology clubs are active but most lack independent websites; coordinate through Aves y Conservación and national ornithology meetings.

groups.name: Aves y Conservación
groups.blurb: The BirdLife partner in Ecuador since 1986, working in key biodiversity areas through conservation and research.

groups.name: Fundación Jocotoco
groups.blurb: Founded 1998 to protect the newly discovered Jocotoco Antpitta, now operating 16 reserves protecting 900 bird species.

groups.name: Comité Ecuatoriano de Registros Ornitológicos (CERO)
groups.blurb: Founded 2011 to establish the official Ecuador bird species list and publish peer reviewed records of bird sightings.

groups.name: Mindo Cloudforest Foundation
groups.blurb: Founded 2001, managing reserves in the Chocó bioregion with over 400 bird species and ecotourism activities.

groups.name: Falklands Conservation
groups.blurb: National conservation organization and BirdLife partner managing nature reserves and seabird monitoring programmes.

groups.name: Falkland Islands Seabird Monitoring Programme
groups.blurb: Citizen science program monitoring penguin, albatross and petrel populations since 1989, visiting colonies regularly.

groups.name: The Watch Group
groups.blurb: Junior citizen science program for ages 8 to 16 with field trips to wildlife sites and conservation badge awards.

name: French Guiana
gaps: Limited formal bird club structure outside of Cayenne area. Faune Guyane ornithological observation platform exists but URL could not be verified (SSL certificate issue).
GEPOG has an active Facebook page as well, left out here because its own site is already listed and one organisation earns one card.

groups.name: GEPOG
groups.blurb: Bird study and protection group managing reserves and conducting ornithological research across French Guiana.

groups.name: Association KWATA
groups.blurb: Founded 1994, focused on study and conservation of fauna and natural habitats in French Guiana's rainforests.

name: Guyana
gaps: No national ornithological society found with BirdLife partnership. Most administrative regions have no dedicated bird clubs or observation programs.

groups.name: Guyana Amazon Tropical Birds Society
groups.blurb: Independent society working with vulnerable youth on ornithological research, education, and bird identification training.

groups.name: South Rupununi Conservation Society
groups.blurb: Conservation organization protecting red siskins and monitoring tropical birds in Guyana's Rupununi savannah region.

name: Paraguay
gaps: Eastern region (Itapúa, Canindeyú, Alto Paraná): birding activity present but no independent clubs with documented websites found. Western Chaco: limited community birding presence documented.
Dropped for lack of a presence of their own: eBird Paraguay (eBird region page, not a community)

groups.name: Guyra Paraguay
groups.blurb: The national bird conservation organisation and BirdLife partner, promoting bird tourism and research.

groups.name: Club de Observadores de la Naturaleza
groups.blurb: National nature observers club founded in 2017, offering identification workshops and citizen science.

groups.name: Club de Observadores de la Naturaleza (Asunción)
groups.blurb: Active birding and nature observer club based in Asunción with regular field outings and education.

name: Peru
gaps: Regional ornithology clubs operate mainly through Facebook and informal networks rather than dedicated websites. COAP has Lima and Cusco chapters but no central site.

groups.name: CORBIDI
groups.blurb: Major research organization promoting bird observation and inclusive birdwatching, maintaining Peru's bird records committee.

groups.name: Unión de Ornitólogos del Perú (UNOP)
groups.blurb: Nonprofit advancing ornithology through congresses, training, and publishing peer reviewed research on Peruvian birds.

groups.name: Club de Observadores de Aves del Perú (COAP)
groups.blurb: Nationwide network of regional birdwatching clubs with chapters in Lima, Cusco and other regions promoting citizen science.

groups.name: Grupo Aves del Perú
groups.blurb: Civil nonprofit institution dedicated to research and conservation of Peru's wild birds through community engagement.

name: Suriname
gaps: No national BirdLife partner or dedicated ornithological society with public membership. Most districts lack organized birding groups.

Suriname Conservation Foundation was left out: it is a government hosted conservation trust fund rather than a community with membership or volunteer birding. Green Heritage Fund is a general wildlife NGO rather than a bird club, kept because it runs the public nature education Suriname birders take part in.

groups.name: Green Heritage Fund Suriname
groups.blurb: Nonprofit promoting sustainable use of natural resources and running wildlife conservation and education programs.

groups.name: Suriname Birds
groups.blurb: Public Facebook group for sharing bird sightings, identification help, and birding experiences in Suriname.

name: Uruguay
gaps: Rural interior departments Salto, Paysandú, Tacuarembó, Florida, Soriano, and others lack documented birding clubs with public presence. Bird watching activity concentrated in Montevideo and coastal departments.
Dropped for lack of a presence of their own: eBird Uruguay (eBird region page, not a community)
Dropped, the social page cited did not exist (soft 404 behind a 200): Club Amigos de las Aves; Birding Uruguay

groups.name: Aves Uruguay
groups.blurb: The national bird society and BirdLife partner, promoting conservation, research and birdwatching.

groups.name: Birdwatching Punta del Este
groups.blurb: Birding community in Punta del Este offering guided walks and environmental education projects.

name: Venezuela
gaps: Website infrastructure for some organizations is limited due to country conditions; primary access through social media and Facebook pages. Many active bird watchers lack formalized club structures.

groups.name: Unión Venezolana de Ornitólogos (UVO)
groups.blurb: Founded 1980, uniting ornithologists and bird enthusiasts to promote study, research and conservation of Venezuelan birds.

groups.name: Fundación Tierra Viva
groups.blurb: Conservation foundation promoting bird observation and biodiversity knowledge through education and citizen science.

groups.name: Sociedad Conservacionista Audubon de Venezuela
groups.blurb: Founded 1970, promoting study, conservation and enjoyment of Venezuelan birds through education and citizen counts.

groups.name: Aves de Venezuela
groups.blurb: Large Facebook community of photography and bird observation enthusiasts sharing field encounters with Venezuelan bird species.
